REACHABILITY_GRAPH.INSTRUCTION_BUILD: Fire enabled transitions in the Petri net to explore the reachability graph step by step.
REACHABILITY_GRAPH.INSTRUCTION_MOVE: Left-click and drag state nodes to customize the layout.
REACHABILITY_GRAPH.INSTRUCTION_RESET: Double-click a state node to reset the Petri net to this marking. Afterwards, firing can be continued from this Petri Net state.
REACHABILITY_GRAPH.INSTRUCTION_VALIDATE: Validate the Reachability Graph and check for completeness. This is based on the current state of the Petri Net and checks whether all transitions that can be fired from the current state have been explored. Does not function while the automatically generated full RG is shown.
REACHABILITY_GRAPH.INSTRUCTION_TOGGLEVIEW: Switches between the view shown in the course script and a view where markings are displayed at each StateNode of the RG.
REACHABILITY_GRAPH.INSTRUCTION_SHOWCOMPLETEGRAPH: With this, the complete Reachability Graph is shown in case of a limited RG. For an unlimited RG, the partial RG up to a critical Marking m' is shown.
REACHABILITY_GRAPH.INSTRUCTION_HIDECOMPLETEGRAPH: Hides the auto-generated complete Reachability Graph and switches view back to the User-generated Graph.

TOUR.WELCOME_TEXT: This guided tour will show you how to create and edit Petri nets. You will learn about the palette, the tuple input, and all the tools at your disposal.
TOUR.PALETTE_TEXT: Use this palette to create new elements. Drag the circle (place) or the rectangle (transition) from the palette onto the canvas to add them to your Petri net.
TOUR.TUPLE_INPUT_TEXT: You can also define your Petri net as a formal tuple, just like in the course text. Type or paste a tuple in the format (P, T, W, m₀) and click 'Generate' to build the net.
TOUR.CANVAS_TEXT: This is your workspace. Elements you drag from the palette appear here. Left-click and drag to move elements around. Middle-click an element or connection to delete it. Double-click an element to rename its label.
TOUR.SCROLL_TEXT: Use the mouse wheel while hovering over a place to increase or decrease its token count. Scroll over a connection (arc) to change its weight.
TOUR.CONNECT_TEXT: To create a connection: right-click on a place or transition to start, then right-click on an element of the opposite type to complete the arc.
TOUR.UPLOAD_TEXT: Click this button to import an existing Petri net file (JSON or PNML format) from your computer.
TOUR.SAVE_TEXT: Click here to export and download your current Petri net as a file.
TOUR.CLEAR_TEXT: This button removes all elements from the canvas, giving you a fresh start.
TOUR.LAYOUT_TEXT: Click this button to automatically rearrange the positions of all elements using a layout algorithm (Spring Embedder or Sugiyama).
TOUR.EXAMPLE_TEXT: Use this menu to load predefined example Petri nets. This is great for getting started or testing features.
TOUR.LANGUAGE_TEXT: Click this button to switch the interface language between English and German.
TOUR.FINISH_TEXT: You now know the basics of creating Petri nets. You can restart this tour anytime using the compass icon in the sidebar.

TOUR.CONSTRUCTION_WELCOME_TEXT: This guided tour will introduce you to the Token Trail construction tab. Here, you will learn how to build Labeled Petri Nets (LPNs) from scratch to validate token trails.
TOUR.PRACTICE_WELCOME_TEXT: This guided tour will introduce you to the Practice tab. Here, you will learn how to validate token trail markings on automatically generated LPNs.
TOUR.LAYOUT_TEXT: The view is split in two: on the left side, you see the original source Petri net. On the right side, you see the Labeled Petri Net (LPN) that you are building or analyzing.
TOUR.BUILD_TEXT: In this mode, you build your own LPN. Drag places or transitions from the left Petri net and drop them onto the canvas on the right. You can connect nodes (right-click transition, then place), delete them, or merge/unmerge overlapping conditions.
TOUR.SOLVE_FILL_TEXT: Click the magic wand button to automatically find and apply a valid token trail marking for all currently empty conditions on the canvas.
TOUR.HIDE_TIPS_TEXT: Toggle this switch to hide live feedback coloring, warning markings, and details. This is useful to test your skills in exam/practice conditions.
TOUR.SET_TOKENS_TEXT:
To configure a token trail for a place in the Petri net:
1. Select a place on the left Petri net.
2. Hover over a condition on the right LPN and scroll the mouse wheel up or down to adjust its token count for that place's trail.
TOUR.STEP_MERGE_TEXT: You can merge conditions to simplify your LPN. Drag one condition directly on top of the other until a blue badge appears, then double-click the group to merge them.
TOUR.STEP_UNMERGE_TEXT: To split merged conditions back, double-click the merged place.
TOUR.STEP_SYNTHESIZE_TEXT: Click the Synthesis button to regenerate the LPN automatically. You can choose between Easy, Medium, Hard, and Expert difficulties. Successfully solving a puzzle on the current difficulty unlocks the next level!
TOUR.STEP_PUZZLE_SOLUTION_TEXT: Stuck? Click this lightbulb button to view the correct token markings for the selected place.
TOUR.FINISH_TEXT: You are ready to explore! You can restart this tour anytime using the help icon (explore compass) in the toolbar.

GOALS.GOAL_SEQUENCE_NET_TOPOLOGY: Structure: Construct your model strictly as a Sequence Net.
GOALS.GOAL_STATE_GRAPH_TOPOLOGY: Structure: Construct your model strictly as a State Graph Net.
GOALS.GOAL_PARTIAL_ORDER_TOPOLOGY: Structure: Construct your model strictly as a Partial Order Net.
GOALS.GOAL_EXPERT_TOPOLOGY: Structure: Construct a general Labeled Petri Net.
GOALS.GOAL_SEQUENCE_PATH: Sequence: Represent a valid path from {{a}} to {{b}}.
GOALS.GOAL_SEQUENCE_PATH_FALLBACK: Path: Ensure there is a path from a start place to any transition.
GOALS.GOAL_ALTERNATIVE_CHOICE: Conflict: Model an alternative choice between event {{y}} and event {{z}}.
GOALS.GOAL_ALTERNATIVE_FALLBACK: Sequence: Ensure event {{y}} is completed before {{z}} starts.
GOALS.GOAL_CONCURRENCY_CHECK: Concurrency: Ensure event {{a}} and event {{b}} can fire concurrently.
GOALS.GOAL_CONCURRENCY_FALLBACK: Loop: Model a loop where event {{a}} can be repeated.
GOALS.GOAL_REPEAT_EVENT: Repeat: Model a path where event {{a}} can fire at least twice.
GOALS.HELP_TEXT_SEQUENCE_NET_TOPOLOGY: A Sequence Net represents a strictly sequential process. It has no branching structures, loops, or concurrency. Transitions must execute one after another in a single line from start to end.
GOALS.HELP_TEXT_PARTIAL_ORDER_TOPOLOGY: A Partial Order Net allows concurrency (transitions firing in parallel) but does not contain loops or conflicts (alternative branches/choices). All parallel paths must eventually sync up.
GOALS.HELP_TEXT_STATE_GRAPH_TOPOLOGY: A State Graph Net allows conflicts (alternative paths or branching choices) and loops, but does not allow concurrent execution (no parallel transitions). Only one transition can fire at a time.
